_comment: Worked example for the two-table model. Shows one Genre, one Document that references it, and several Statement Assessments that reference the Document. Illustrates that a single Encyclical carries passages at different registers: most of the text at the genre default (authentic-ordinary), while three central moral judgments rise to the ordinary and universal magisterium. Editorial 'topic' fields are paraphrases, not quotations.

genre.label: Encyclical
genre.description: Circular letter of the pope to the universal Church; can invoke the ordinary and universal magisterium.

assessments.topic: The encyclical as a whole: exhortation and doctrinal synthesis on the value and inviolability of human life.

provenance.note: Default register inherited from the genre; the three moral judgments below are the exceptions.

assessments.topic: The direct and voluntary killing of an innocent human being is always gravely immoral.

provenance.note: Confirmed 'by the authority which Christ conferred upon Peter and his Successors, in communion with the Bishops' — i.e. by the ordinary and universal magisterium. Primary-vs-secondary object debated.

assessments.topic: Direct abortion, as an end or a means, is always gravely immoral.

provenance.note: Declared taught 'by the ordinary and universal Magisterium.'

assessments.topic: Euthanasia is a grave violation of the law of God.

provenance.note: Taught 'in harmony with the Magisterium of my Predecessors and in communion with the Bishops.' Object classification debated.
